reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its normed additive group structure. For every natural number n with dim_R(E) = n + 1, every x on the unit sphere S = {u in E : ||u|| = 1}, every function f : E -> R, and every vector g in E, suppose f has a genuine ambient Frechet derivative at x represented by v |-> <g,v>. Put L = (R x)^perp. Then for every candidate z in L the following are equivalent:
(1) For every abstract tangent vector w in T_x S, using the real n-dimensional manifold model, the differential of the restricted function f|_S at x evaluated on w equals <d(iota)_x(w), z>, where iota : S -> E is the literal inclusion and z is coerced into E for the pairing.
(2) z is exactly the orthogonal projection of g onto L, with both sides regarded as elements of L.
Thus the projection is the unique vector in the orthogonal complement of x that represents the restricted differential through the inner product induced by the inclusion. The pairing uses the ambient image d(iota)_x(w); it does not identify the candidate's subtype with the abstract tangent type by an unstated equality. The differential expressions are the specified mvfderiv operators, which return zero when differentiability is absent. In this sphere setting the ambient HasGradientAt hypothesis gives differentiability of the restriction at x, and the inclusion is differentiable, so the characterization concerns genuine differentials at that point, rather than freely supplied linear maps or a condition that holds merely because a nondifferentiable map has a totalized zero derivative.
The claim is local at x. It assumes no global smoothness of f, imposes no positivity or nonzero condition on g or z, and includes n = 0 (ambient dimension one). It asserts an exact iff for all candidates z, not just that the projected candidate satisfies the pairing identity. It gives no differential equation, convergence bound, global gradient field, or formula for derivatives away from x.
objects: E: finite-dimensional real normed inner-product space; S: its unit sphere; x: a point of S; f: an arbitrary real-valued function on E; g: an ambient gradient at x; L: the orthogonal complement of the real span of x; z: an element of L; w: an abstract tangent vector at x; iota: the literal inclusion S -> E.
domains: n is in N and dim_R(E)=n+1; x is in Metric.sphere (0:E) 1; f is in E -> R; g is in E; z is in (R x)^perp; w is in TangentSpace (R-model n) x. Values of the restricted differential and of the inner product are real. d(iota)_x(w) is an ambient vector in E; orthogonalProjectionOnto g has subtype L.
quantifiers: Universal E with NormedAddCommGroup E, InnerProductSpace R E, and FiniteDimensional R E; universal n:N with Fact(dim_R(E)=n+1); universal x:S, f:E->R, g:E; implication from HasGradientAt f g x; then universal z:L; inside the left side of the iff, universal w:T_x S. The right side contains no w. There is no separately quantified abstract tangent candidate and no existential hypothesis.
assumptions: Real normed inner-product and finite-dimensional structures on E; exact ambient dimension n+1; x has norm one; HasGradientAt f g x certifies the ambient Frechet derivative v |-> <g,v>. Membership of z in L is enforced by its type. No global regularity of f is assumed.
conclusion: For every z:L, [for every w:T_x S, mvfderiv of f restricted to S at x on w = <mvfderiv of iota at x on w, coercion(z)>] iff [z = L.orthogonalProjectionOnto g]. Both directions are asserted. Consequently the projected candidate exists and is the unique candidate satisfying the representation condition.
scopes: The gradient assumption governs the whole forall-z equivalence. Both differentials are evaluated at the same sphere point x under the model indexed by n. The equality on the right is in the orthogonal-complement subtype, whereas the inner product on the left is in E. All claims concern this one point; the statement does not posit a global manifold gradient field. mvfderiv is totalized to zero outside differentiability, but ambient differentiability and smooth sphere inclusion make the present characterization about actual differentials.
constant_dependencies: The only numerical constants in the statement are the sphere center 0, radius 1, and dimension increment 1. The manifold model depends on n; the orthogonal subspace depends on E and x; the projected vector depends on E, x, and g. No rate constants, measures, or external parameters occur.
